# OpenBar agent instructions

## First action for inspecting or editing a project

Discover the tool catalog and call get_project_state before inspecting project
content or answering "how would you edit this card?". Hypothetical edit questions
require read-only discovery and an exact tool-based plan. An actual requested
change authorizes the corresponding write.

Browser JavaScript on the project page:
1. await window.openbarAgent.listTools()
2. await window.openbarAgent.executeTool("get_project_state", {detail: "full"})
3. await window.openbarAgent.executeTool("get_mindmap", {})
4. Inspect the returned nodes and patch_mindmap_node input schema.
5. Describe the edit using patch_mindmap_node with id, expectedRevision, and the
   requested title/text fields. On an actual edit request, execute that call,
   check ok, then read get_mindmap again to verify persistence.
Use the returned node identity to resolve "first card". State your interpretation.
TODO card title/text edits use the paper TODO tool described in the catalog.

For HTTP MCP or REST, the equivalent card reads/writes also require project
(the URL segment after /p/) and mapId from get_project_state. Read the selected
transport's schema. A browser revision and a saved-state revision can differ.

A web-reader URL safety error is specific to that reader. Try a reachable local
HTTP client or browser JavaScript transport. Browser JavaScript can use the
window.openbarAgent bridge in a standard browser. Headless clients can use
authenticated REST immediately, or initialize the MCP connection below.
With an authorized local checkout, use the configured OPENBARRY_ACCESS_TOKEN
from the process environment or .env.local, keeping its value private.
Report the attempted transport and exact connection error when blocked.

Use UI interaction for visual verification and capabilities beyond the tool
catalog. For supported card edits, give the tool name, node ID, concurrency
fields, changed fields, and verification step in your answer.

OpenBar edits repository-backed research papers and their mindmaps.

Human and agent guide: /agents
Project URLs: /p/<project-slug>/mindmap and /p/<project-slug>/paper
Agent discovery: every page includes visually hidden MCP and WebMCP instructions
in its initial HTML and accessibility tree, plus HTTP Link headers to this guide.
The "MCP / WebMCP" button on project pages shows the registered tools.

Browser agents: use a WebMCP integration supporting document.modelContext or navigator.modelContext on
HTTPS or localhost. Discover the active page's registered tools through the
integration. Start with get_project_state, detail="full", then search_project
and navigate_project. The current page supplies the project identity.

Headless MCP clients: use Streamable HTTP at /api/mcp on this origin.
Authentication is required: Authorization: Bearer <OPENBARRY_ACCESS_TOKEN>,
or an allowed Cloudflare Access identity. Ask the workspace owner for credentials.
Initialize, retain Mcp-Session-Id, send notifications/initialized, then tools/list.
Call get_project_state with {"project":"<project-slug>","detail":"full"}.
Read AGENTS.md and useful project skills returned by project state.
Use returned IDs, revisions, and hashes for writes. Check local persistence and
remote synchronization receipts separately.

Git conflicts: get_project_state includes sync status, local/base/remote
commit IDs, changed paths, and Git recovery refs. Call sync_project with
{"action":"inspect","refresh":true}, then {"action":"review_pull"} to prepare
a review. HTTP MCP also requires project="<slug>". The review returns its token
and the base, local, and remote contents for every conflicting file. Apply with
{"action":"apply_pull","token":"...","resolutions":[{"path":"main.tex","choice":"merged","text":"<complete file>"}]}.
Choices local and remote select the entire saved file. cancel_pull closes a
review. A changed local HEAD or tracked working tree requires a fresh review.
Reviews operate on saved repository files. Save live browser drafts first.
Force pull and force push in the human interface require two confirmations and
preserve both Git versions under refs/openbar/recovery. Force push checks the
reviewed remote commit with a lease.

The canvas stays visible while Unplaced TODOs are dragged from the side tray
onto a parent card. Priority uses Clear/P0/P1/P2/P3 buttons. Progress uses Clear
and seven pie states. Ordinary cards support Plain, Markdown (including tables),
and TeX. Each card holds one image. Paste or drop an image onto a card or its
editor. Further images become child cards. Click the image for the full viewer.
Drag its corner to resize, or use its focused resize handle's arrow keys.
Use patch_mindmap_node with refs[].imageWidth (25–100 percent) to resize through
tools. Preserve the reference's other fields. To attach another image through
tools, create a child with add_mindmap_node, then attach_mindmap_image there.
Removing an image detaches its reference and preserves the shared project asset.
Undo restores the image. A multi-image paste is one undo step.

Portable browser automation: await window.openbarAgent.executeTool(name, args).
Discover full schemas with window.openbarAgent.listTools(). This bridge works
in standard browsers and exposes the same live page operations as native WebMCP.
After navigate_project returns status="scheduled", await
window.openbarAgent.waitForNavigation(result.value.href) before page-local calls.

REST clients: GET /api/tools for schemas, POST /api/tools/<tool-name> with a JSON
arguments object. GET /api/projects lists projects. GET /openapi.json supplies
OpenAPI 3.1 discovery. Use the same bearer authentication as HTTP MCP.
MCP structuredContent, its text content, REST and browser operations all use
{ok:true,value,...} or {ok:false,code,message,retryable,...} result envelopes.
Call get_agent_capabilities for current headless tools and transport details.
HTTP operations use saved-state hashes. Browser operations may require live
editor revisions. Read the schema of the selected transport before writing.

Stdio-only clients: run node scripts/mcp-stdio.mjs from the OpenBar checkout,
with OPENBARRY_URL=https://<your-host> and OPENBARRY_ACCESS_TOKEN in the child
process environment. Use node directly to keep stdout strictly JSON-RPC.
The bridge uses the same HTTP endpoint and saved-state operations.

MCP supports protocol versions 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25.
Keep the negotiated version and session header on subsequent calls. A session
expires after 30 minutes of inactivity. On HTTP 404 initialize a fresh session.
GET /api/mcp returns 405 because this server uses JSON responses. Read job state
with get_paper_compile. Resources and prompts are available through MCP.

Network: Tailscale addresses require the client's machine to join the private
network. Cloud-hosted clients require an owner-configured reachable deployment.
Browser agents on another origin require OPENBARRY_AGENT_ORIGINS and the correct
embedding tools permission. Authorization remains required for HTTP calls.
OAuth-only clients require an external identity-provider deployment. The current
bearer-token setup supports headless clients directly and through the stdio bridge.

Card authorship: Write every card as self-contained material for an external reader, including cards prompted by @agent or @agents. State the question or topic, essential context, answer or current uncertainty, and relevant evidence or file references. Keep conversational replies and personal acknowledgments in the task. Preserve the project-specific meaning and available evidence.
Agent-created cards stay marked Agent draft through edits and refreshes. The human
accepts them using the small Save card control at the upper right, or deletes them.
Extended notes open in a floating window beside the card.
When Git has incoming commits or conflicts, review and synchronize to resume editing.
